recipes.name: Crustless Spinach Quiche
ingredients_raw: 1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach - thawed, drained, and squeezed dry

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease a 9-inch pie pan.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add onions and cook, stirring occasionally, until soft, about 3 minutes. Stir in spinach and continue to cook until excess moisture has evaporated.
Whisk together eggs, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Add Muenster cheese and spinach mixture and stir until well blended.
Bake in the preheated oven until eggs have set, about 30 minutes.
Remove from the oven and let cool for 10 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Crustless Spinach Quiche
raw_recipe.description: This crustless quiche made with eggs, spinach, and Muenster cheese is quick and easy to bake in just 30 minutes for a delicious breakfast or brunch.

review.reviewBody: Instead of one large quiche, I pour the mixture into the bottoms of a greased muffin pan, a little less than half full. It makes bite sized portions that are perfect for a party. My friends always ask me for "my recipe"! Easy and delicious. Oh, I use whatever shredded cheese is on sale at the store.

I've adapted this recipe to be a bit healthier - I use EggBeaters in place of the eggs, use lowfat feta cheese and I put in a bit of chopped lean ham. I bake them in muffin tins and two muffin sized mini quiches are less than 100 calories (2 points if you're a Weight Watcher!). I slightly under cook them so I can pop them in the microwave at work for a nice breakfast.

Yummy! I didn't use muenster cheese. Instead, to make this lower fat, I used 3 eggs, 1/2 cup light sharp cheddar, 1 cup fat free cottage cheese, and a 1/4 cup light parmesan cheese. I added a few sliced mushrooms and green onion in the saute. Although not as rich, still tasty and forgiving recipe.

I made this nearly every Friday during Lent and my whole family loves it. Sometimes I would vary it a little, using fresh spinach, adding mushrooms or green peppers or an extra egg. I always doubled the pepper and used fresh cracked. This is a fantastic recipe and very versatile.
I have been making this quiche for many years. It is so easy and delicious. I use a good sharp Cheddar cheese.

I made these in regular muffin tins it was enough to make about 14 muffin size quiches. There were done at about 25 minutes. I made a few in mini muffin tins just to test it and these turned out great too and were done in about 20 minutes. (My oven usually takes a few extra minutes to cook things). I brought these to a brunch with 6 people and they were gone in about 3 minutes, before we even sat down to eat.

Update: I made again recently and substituted 1 cup of cheese with one cup of cottage cheese. It worked great and you would have never known there was cottage cheese in them. Since cottage cheese is denser I got a few extra "muffins" (18 exactly)

Love this as a base recipe. You can add pretty much whatever you like to the base to make it your own. My first cooking included chopped green chiles and jalepeno peppers. I then sliced cherry tomatoes to garnish on top before going in the oven, and served with sour cream and salsa. It was beautiful and was a HUGE success. Everyone had seconds. My second cooking had a Greek flair. I used Feta cheese, added chopped artichoke hearts, oregano, six large shrimp arranged on top as a garnish, etc. I say "etc." because you really can custom this to ANY taste you desire. Only hard fast rules are to use 6 eggs instead of the suggested 5, and depending on the ingredients you opt in, you will have to adjust the cooking time up -- check in 3-5 minute intervals until a knife comes out clean. Have fun! Experiment. It's all good!

This is probably one of my favorite foods. I could eat it every day and not get tired of it! The only changes I make are using fresh spinach (melt the butter in the skillet, cook the onions in the butter, add 10 ounces fresh spinach until wilted; let cool slightly and chop with a knife on a cutting board) and using whatever cheese I have on hand (usually cheddar; I've actually never tried it with Muenster cheese). I've also mixed in fresh, firm, diced tomatoes and it's good. This is a spring/summer standby in our house; even two out of my three kids love it.

I would give this recipe a 4.5, but a 5 with these changes - I cut the spinach down by almost a half. All of the spinach was too much and made it too dense. I also added two finely crushed fresh garlic cloves, added about 1/2 cup of shredded parmesan, and about two tablespoons of finely diced red peppers. I also used the mini muffin pan since this was for a brunch party. I first filled them 3/4 of the way and they turned out too dry so the next time I filled them to the top and they puffed up perfectly and they were so moist and fluffy. It took about 25 minutes at 350 degrees. They were such a hit and they popped out just perfectly!! Thanks for the recipe.

My tip for this delicious recipe? Sprinkle 1/4 cup of shredded parmesan cheese on top of the quiche before it goes in the oven. This will add a slightly browned, crispy crust on top that adds a little texture, and makes for a beautiful presentation!

Perfect! Used a suggestion to pour the mixture in muffin forms for mini-quiche - instant hit! No additions/alterations required, except for one: add some feta cheese to the mix! Goes wonerful with spinach!

I used mozzarella cheese instead of Muenster, because that's what I had on hand. I added mushrooms and a green pepper and parsley from the garden. I used fresh spinach. After you soften the onion, green pepper, and mushrooms, add the fresh spinach to the mixture on the stove. It cooks down quickly. I like that it is pastry free as I am trying to watch my carbs!! Good keto recipe!! Easy and quick.

for whatever reason, I found this recipe just 'meh'. I used fresh baby spinach and domestic Swiss cheese and added a little nutmeg because it pairs well with spinach. Despite this I found the quiche greasy and pretty tasteless. I won't make this again.

Followed the recipe except for a few of changes: mozzarella cheese, cheddar cheese, fresh spinach, 1 cup fresh crab. Shared with neighbors. It was a hit! The quichewas gone before I though about getting a picture.
So easy and really delicious. I added just a smidge of nutmeg and dry ground mustard-also mushrooms because they were in the fridge. It’s a keeper.

I made this recipe just as it is written, except I used a muffin pan instead of a baking pan. It turned out perfectly. Next time, I added my own ingredients and added different cheeses, and again, perfect. It took about 20-25 minutes on 350 degrees for my oven in the muffin pan.

This is the best Quiche recipe I have found. We loved it. Leftovers did not hang around long. I used a variety of white cheeses with some sharp cheddar. I also put tomato slices on the top for decoration. This will be made quite often here!

So easy and adaptable. I use whatever I have, including ham, bacon, sausage crumbles. Any cheese will work as well. I've even done chopped tomato, spinach and mozzarella. Delicious with any combination
Easy to make and taste good, great for a fast meal.

I love this recipe. I used Munster cheese, Cracker Barrel, natural cheddar a block of Gouda and a half a container of feta tomato basil and then I added a 16 ounce can of crab meat lump. It was delicious. You can freeze it and eat it with a little salsa on top it’ll change your life.
